Hi all — I pulled the headers Priyom attached and compared with a successful invite flow. Two things stand out:
1) The corporate proxy is rewriting the X-Forwarded-For and inserting an X-Proxy-User header we don't normally see. That can break our short-lived OTP nonce mapping when the request path relies on client IP affinity.
2) The request from the customer shows a truncated Cookie header (we see only part of the session cookie). When the session cookie gets truncated by intermediate proxies or WAFs the server fails to correlate the OTP request with the original invite session and returns a 202 that never resolves client-side.

Workarounds:
- Short term: Priyom can create a manual activation token and send it via email (expires in 24h). This avoids the browser-side OTP flow.
- Medium term: Customer IT should whitelist outbound POSTs to api.redwood-inference.com/auth/otp and preserve the full Cookie and X-Forwarded-* headers. We can provide exact CIDR ranges and a sample allowlist entry.

I'll attach a small log snippet showing the truncated cookie and the proxy headers for the Ops ticket.

--
